name: Average Basics: Equal Share, Total and Missing Values
description: See an average as an equal share, move quickly between mean and total, and recover missing values or counts.
script_scope: Teach Average = Sum ÷ Number through an equal-share picture, then reverse it to Sum = Average × Number and Number = Sum ÷ Average. Use direct lists, missing observations, two-number and ratio-based averages, and simple unknown-count questions. Show that changing every observation by the same addition, subtraction or multiplication changes the mean in the same way. Finish with a capstone where only part of a data set changes, so the learner must update the total rather than blindly shift the mean. Every answer should be checked by rebuilding the total.

name: Consecutive and Patterned Averages
description: Use symmetry to average consecutive numbers, odd/even runs, natural numbers, multiples and filtered sequences without long addition.
script_scope: Teach the centre-of-a-balanced-list idea first: an odd equally spaced list averages to its middle term, while an even list averages to the midpoint of its two middle terms or endpoints. Extend this to consecutive integers, consecutive odd/even numbers, the first n natural numbers and the first n multiples of a number. Then handle numbers in an interval that satisfy a condition by identifying the correct list before averaging. End by showing how the average moves when the next terms of a consecutive sequence are appended.

name: Weighted and Frequency Averages
description: Average values that occur different numbers of times or carry different importance by turning each value into its total contribution.
script_scope: Teach weighted average as total contribution divided by total weight. Build from repeated values to unequal group sizes, frequency tables using class midpoints, examination weights, subject weights and quantities bought at different unit prices. Show why simply averaging subgroup means works only when their weights are equal. Include an unknown weighted component where the overall mean is known. The learner should repeatedly use value × weight, add the contributions, add the weights, then divide once.

name: Combined Groups and Group Ratios
description: Combine group means and work backward to find an unknown group mean, size, ratio or percentage.
script_scope: Teach combined averages by converting each subgroup mean to a subgroup total. Work backward to find an unknown subgroup mean or subgroup size. Then derive the two-group balance/alligation idea: the combined mean lies between the two group means, and the group-size ratio is obtained from the opposite gaps. Use this to find ratios, percentages and passed/failed or boys/girls counts. Finish with a three-group capstone where one combined mean first reveals an internal ratio.

name: Missing, Overlapping and Partial Averages
description: Recover hidden observations from partial averages, overlapping groups and repeated middle values.
script_scope: Teach partial-average questions by converting every stated mean into a sum and marking which observations each subtotal contains. Cover a hidden middle value, an unmentioned remainder, overlapping first-k and last-k groups where one observation is counted twice, overlapping day/temperature windows, pairwise averages, and direct subtraction of overlapping windows. Include a data-sufficiency checkpoint showing that group means alone may not determine a combined mean without group sizes. End with a capstone that combines subset totals with relative differences among the remaining observations.

name: Adding, Removing, Replacing and Correcting Observations
description: Track the total when members enter, leave, are replaced, or when a recorded value is corrected.
script_scope: Teach all membership changes through totals. For adding or removing a member, compare the old and new total. For a same-size replacement, show that change in total = number of observations × change in mean = new value − old value. Extend to groups entering or leaving. For wrong entries, repair the recorded total by subtracting the wrong value and adding the correct value, including two-error cases. Finish with the common replacement shortcut that recovers the outgoing member from the mean shift.

name: Age Averages Through Time
description: Treat age averages as changing age totals while carefully updating both elapsed time and family or class membership.
script_scope: Teach that when the same people remain together, every age and therefore the average rises by the same number of years. Convert past averages to present totals, then handle a teacher joining, one person leaving, replacement, a birth, and average changes stated in months. Use short timelines and update the count whenever membership changes. Finish with a marriage-and-child timeline where the learner must separate years before the child was born from the child's present age.

name: Average Rates, Prices and Productivity
description: Average quotients correctly by returning each displayed rate to the real total amount and real total quantity behind it.
script_scope: Teach why displayed rates often cannot be averaged directly. Cover equal quantities bought at different prices, equal money spent at different prices, kg-per-rupee buying rates, workers with different completion times converted to units per minute, different day types with different visitor counts, charges weighted by attendance ratios, and the fixed-plus-variable boarding-expense pattern from the exercise. End with a petrol-cost capstone where equal money is spent at several prices, so litres purchased become the correct denominator.

name: Cricket, Scores and Changing Performance Averages
description: Turn innings, run rates, bowling figures and exam averages back into totals before making the next change.
script_scope: Teach performance averages through the same total-first habit. Cover a new innings changing a batting average, finding the required next score, removing highest and lowest scores, target run rate after completed overs, a captain scoring above the average of teammates, bowling average after new wickets, examination-paper averages changed by bonus marks, and a team-score capstone where one score is hypothetically changed. Always distinguish old count from new count.

name: Average Speed for Equal Distances
description: Understand why equal-distance journeys use a harmonic-style average, derive 2xy/(x+y), and know when not to use it.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's equal-distance formula Average speed = 2xy/(x+y) by first comparing actual travel times on a short out-and-back journey. Show why the simple arithmetic mean is wrong because the slower leg lasts longer. Derive the formula from total distance ÷ total time, practise direct substitution and solving for a missing return speed, use speed ratios, and build a sanity check that the result lies between the two speeds and below their arithmetic mean when the speeds differ. Explicitly contrast equal-distance and unequal-distance journeys; unequal distances must return to total distance ÷ total time.
